title: Two shims that request each other at once both get answered
intention: Two shims that request each other over the bus at the same moment never deadlock: each delivery's reply is posted without holding the sender shim's lock while it waits on the recipient's.
why: Law 7 (errors are loud): a deadlock is a silent 900s hang (_TIMEOUT_S in cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py), not an error anybody sees; and the telos aim that devices are peers that can lean on each other over the bus (Law 8: a peer is leaned on, and a bus that can freeze two peers cannot be).
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud): a deadlock is a silent 900s hang (_TIMEOUT_S in cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py), not an error anybody sees; and the telos aim that devices are peers that can lean on each other over the bus (Law 8: a peer is leaned on, and a bus that can freeze two peers cannot be).
how: In the bus server (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py), a shim's delivery hook runs inside that shim's RLock, and the reply or request it posts takes the recipient shim's lock in the same thread: lock order A then B in one thread, B then A in another. Measured stacks: thread 87721 holds codemother's lock (on_commit -> watch._escalate_to_hex -> request to inference_domain) and waits on inference_domain's; thread 87808 holds inference_domain's (an infer from a proof -> _check_mail delivers codemother's queued request -> shim.py:815 posts the reply to codemother) and waits on codemother's. First cut: posts made from inside a locked delivery are queued and delivered after the shim's lock is released (or delivery to another shim never happens under the caller's lock). A proof drives two shims that request each other concurrently and asserts both answer inside a bound. Builder notes: Questions a Haiku builder would need: (a) Where are the locks? cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py lines 90, 106-116 (the `locked` wrapper) and 241. (b) Where does the second acquisition happen? bus.py:450, where post() calls the recipient's delivery hook synchronously in the posting thread. (c) How do I make two shims for a proof? Copy the scratch-bus pattern the existing proofs in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ use (a bus server under a scratch home with two held test shims); never the live bus. (d) What counts as answered? request() returns a reply envelope whose body is the handler's dict. (e) How do I avoid hanging the test suite on the red? Each try runs in a thread joined with a 10s timeout, and a try that does not join counts as hung. All five are answered in this packet and ride the ticket's how.
falsifier: Falsifier: a proof under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ makes two bus-hosted scratch shims send each other requests at the same moment and sees both answered inside 10s on 20 of 20 tries; against the pre-fix server.py at least one try hangs past the bound (hollow red). The existing bus proofs stay green, including the 48519f4789b1 property that one shim's hook never runs on two threads at once. Horizon: this ticket's PROVED.
watchme: none, because the recurrence watch is the proof itself: bin/cairn test --seal reruns every proof under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ whenever cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py or bus.py changes, so a regression reds at the commit that causes it
